children: Russia's services sector returned to growth in August for the first time in six months, helped by renewed increases in output and new sales amid stronger customer demand, a business survey showed on Thursday.
The S&P Global Russia Services PMI Business Activity Index rose to 51.3 in August from 49.0 in July. The 50 mark separates growth from contraction.

New business also returned to growth after four months of decline, with the increase the quickest since February, though S&P Global said the pace was only fractional. New export orders expanded for the first time since March.

Employment fell for a seventh straight month, but the decline was the slowest in three months. Outstanding business also contracted for a fifth successive month, although the pace of depletion eased to only a slight rate.

Cost pressures eased, with input price inflation at the joint-slowest pace in 2026 so far, matching June. Output charge inflation, however, accelerated for a second month and was the fastest since March.
Firms' optimism about the year-ahead outlook strengthened for a third straight month and reached its highest since March, supported by hopes of stronger demand and planned advertising investment.
The composite output index rose to 50.6 from 49.6, signalling private sector activity expanded for the first time in six months.
